text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- President Martti Ahtisaari says Finland's geographical location as neighbour to Russia is no longer a determining factor in its international cooperation.
- Alko to stop importing Czech brand Budejovicky Budvar beer in face of threatened law suit by makers of U.S. Budweiser beer.
- Forty-five percent of women who have silicon breast implants say they are satisfied with the operation, survey shows. @
- Regional differences in unemployment have widened considerably. The area worst affected is Lapland where a quarter of the population is unemployed.
- Setting his mind on 1998 state budget, Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto wants to have a close look at planned spending.
- State-owned Postipankki plans to boost its market share in stockbroking, says in coming head of treasury Ari Aaltonen, currently chief economist. @
- Successful corporate communication can enable companies to influence the way they are presented in media, says Nokia's newly appointed head of corporate communications Lauri Kivinen.

- Social Democrat Party MPs agreed to assume group discipline in vote on liberalised opening hours for retailers. Parliamentary group leader Erkki Tuomioja expects proposal to be passed in final vote on Thursday of Friday. @
- Uniquely well-preserved middle-age musical notes found in Helsinki University archives.
- Meteorologists forecast a white christmas for all of Finland.
